previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of chronic alcohol use, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and prior strokes was admitted with fever, cough, and chest pain concerning for pneumonia. Community-acquired pneumonia was treated with antibiotics, and imaging confirmed left lower lobe involvement. During the hospitalization, he developed hyponatremia due to SIADH, likely exacerbated by hypothyroidism (TSH ~20), leading to fluid restriction and increased levothyroxine. He had recurrent fevers attributed to aspiration, confirmed by a video swallow study showing aspiration of thin liquids; he was placed on a nectar-thick diet. Abdominal pain was linked to severe constipation and a gastric ulcer with pyloric deformity found on EGD. Electrolyte abnormalities consistent with refeeding syndrome were managed with supplementation. A PICC line was placed for reliable access. He remained in normal sinus rhythm, and diltiazem was held due to low blood pressure. He improved clinically, was stabilized, and discharged home with services and multiple follow-up appointments.
problems: Syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone
Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
Other disorders of electrolyte and fluid balance, not elsewhere classified
Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit

PROCEDURE:  1. Repositioning of right PICC.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the existing
PICC line was aspirated and flushed and a Nitinol guidewire was introduced
into the superior vena cava (SVC). A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior vena cava. A
single lumen PIC line measuring 37 cm in length was then placed through the
peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic
guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film
of the chest. The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The
catheter was secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. Existing right arm approach PICC with tip in the right internal jugular
vein replaced with a new single lumen PIC line with tip at the cavoatrial
junction.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a 37 cm right arm approach single lumen PowerPICC with
tip at the cavoatrial junction.  The line is ready to use.
